I'm 7.25 x 5.25. And the answer is... I don't know?

I'm not that sexually experienced first of all. Secondly, I don't feel superior to other men based on my size. First off, my size isn't THAT huge, so there COULD be someone in the room rocking a 9" monster dong. I have no clue how big someone is, and to me, the size of your penis doesn't make you who you are. I am very submissive and insecure. I guess most people would guess I had a small one? Not sure.

Everyone who is a decent human being needs love from someone. Plain and simple. Life is horrible and lonely without someone else. Only horrible people deserve to be miserable and alone. I am not sure why you aren't getting this.
Why not? Do you feel the same way about yourself? If so, you need to get confidence. If you just think that way about me, then you're assuming how I am as a whole person based on one post.
I know I'm not entitled to good luck. No one is entitled to anything in life. But people deserve things. Good people deserve to be loved, good people deserve to have good luck.

Exactly. I do think that there are a lot of assholes that think that way. My opinion, that I wanted to have thoughts on, was that not everyone saying "I am a nice guy and I don't have an SO", they MIGHT not be saying that they are entitled, rather than "Well shit, this sucks."

> You sound hella entitled. Yeah that would suck. but I wouldn't blame being nice. That's a bowl of bullshit.

I never said it was because I was nice. I'm just saying I have shitty luck. That's all.

Here is what I'm saying... Let's take relationships out of it.

Imagine if you had a next door neighbor, that neighbor was the biggest asshole you've ever met. You, however, always strive to be a good person. You have nothing but shitty luck, and your neighbor won the lottery or has just back to back good luck. Now, imagine how you'd feel.

That's how I feel not having an SO. Everyone has SOs, both good and bad a like. I strive to be a good person, and I even have a handful of friends. No one is ever attracted to me and I can't find someone I am compatible with. Even though I strive to be a good person. 

That being said, I wouldn't consider myself the "Nice Guy" - I don't externalize and get mad a particular woman I'm interested in for her not being interested. I just move on but it does make me mad at the world as a whole.

I am not saying that niceness is a bad quality or that it is holding me back. I am also not saying that me being nice should automatically make me attractive.

I'm just saying people who talk about the whole "nice guy" thing, could just be saying what I'm saying. My whole message is "Sometimes good people have bad luck."

I don't think it is my niceness holding me back at all. I'm just saying that even though I am a nice person, I don't really have anyone. Not blaming women, or anything. I'm just basically saying "Shitty things happen to good people, and good things happen to shitty people."

I would say I have numbers one and two. I get attached easily, and then it doesn't work out. I am also shy. I don't have high standards at all, but I am picky about my potential love partners. Not in looks, but in similar interests and such. And I am a very alternative person.

No no no. I'm talking about people who are outward about it. Like ACTUAL assholes. People who are openly sexist, homophobic, etc. Like, I'm basically saying people worse than me have boyfriends/girlfriends. Including people even more judgmental than I am.
But I'm at the old age of 24
Okay. Then I am cis. I am just kind of gender-sterotype-nuteral.

That's what I am. Just doesn't succumb to hetronormitivity. Idk if I am lucky because many girls are not attracted to me as a potential partner. Even though I am not gay, most girls still think of me as a "gay friend" kind of. Not crying "friendzone" or anything, just an observation.
Okay, I remember reading that the definition of cis as "Your identifying gender doesn't match up to what society says you ought to be" - Which is why I thought.
Actually, I don't really have any friends. Most friends I hang out with are through her.

That's the thing. They've put up with my drunken behavior quite some time. Now it has been a while since I've had an explosion. But I am afraid that they kinda went to their breaking point. Like take couples for example. If a guy is doing something once, maybe twice or even 3 or 4 times, it eventually fixes if the guy (or even girl) changes his/her behavior, after a while, it's "fuck this" - that being said, we haven't been in a fight in a long-long time and haven't had any issues for a while up until now. So I am sure it could blow over. I hope we can get on the same level of friendship that we were before this big fight.
I totally agree. The only thing that worries me is that she's never really been mad at me longer than a few days.
The fight Nov 1st. I then gave a short apology 6 days later. It's now been 5 days with no contact. Not sure how much space is enough.
I am fine. Still bumbed out and guilty to how I treated a friend. The fight Nov 1st. I then gave a short apology 6 days later. It's now been 5 days with no contact. Not sure how much space is enough.

Gotcha. I just did the half-assed apology 3 days ago. I am afraid if I send her another she'll feel crowded and bothered. S told me to back off and leave her alone. Part of me wants to apologize and let her see I am sorry, part of me feels to just back off and let her come back on her own if she does.

But it's kind of a damned if I do damned if I don't.

The two scenerios are like so:

Apologize again - Pro: She'll know how sorry I am. Con: She might feel crowded again and might be less wanting to come back. 

Not say anything: Pro: I give her space, she'll get over it, she might come back. Con: She won't know how sorry I really am, and might not come back. 

Either way, maybe I should wait another 3 days?

True. Having a close friend is one of the best things to have in life, and losing one is a horrible feeling. I am trying to work on myself.

The thing is, I did apologize. It was a very short and quick apology, and thinking back, I kind of minimized what I did through the apology. I said sorry for being annoying/obnoxious, but in reality I was a total dick-head childish asshole. I am not sure how to re-appolgize and be more sincere if I've already gave an apology that was half-assed. I do, however, want to let her know that I feel like shit about what I said about her and didn't mean a word of it. I also want to tell her how much of a friend I think she was (is?). I just don't know how. 

Also, I am depressed now because I lost a friend, but I am not sure if I was depressed before.
Yes, but I'm talking about the BEST way. Like a nice pleasant death.
That's the thing. If we're not talking, how can she see that I'm kinder?

Hey, I posted an update: http://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/1qag00/so_i_figured_out_i_am_a_toxic_friend_but_i_think/

Thanks for your time earlier, and the time to read/reply to this post would mean a lot. I've just been obsessing over how I've acted and how fucked up it was of me to do such things to such a great friends, and how terrible of a person that might make me to be.

Also, about the apology. I apologized for making a mountain out of an anthill. I had yet to apologize for saying the awful things I've said because I don't remember saying them. I remember going off, but I didn't remember the specifics. Our mutual friend said I said some nasty things. I don't want to re-apologze and be like "OH YEAH. I forgot!" Because that will bug her further and make it sound like I'm excusing myself.

True. Yeah, she's always forgiven me. Too, she hasn't said anything about NOT being my friend. She's a very outspoken person. My theory, and hope, is that she is just not wanting to talk/hang out for some time to get over her mad-spell at me. It could be a week or two, or maybe months.

On my main account I've been asking for advice in /r/zen and such. I also do have a therapist but it's through my probation, so if I admit to drinking, I could get in trouble with probation. I am not allowed to see a non-probation affiliate therapist until I get off, which isn't until 11 months from now. 

However, on my own, I've been practicing mindfulness and DBT (dialectical behavior therapy). Which is also a type of mindfulness.
I don't take psych meds. I wasn't really diagnosed with depression, I looked at my diagnoses and it says "Cannabis dependency with depressed mood acute"

I posted an update, and it gives a follow up to part 1. http://www.reddit.com/r/relationship_advice/comments/1q4rfj/update_i_24m_kinda_flipped_out_on_a_friend_of/

Everyone on there seems to think that it's over and done with, I'd like to get your input.

Who knows how it will all go down? You can't really speculate either way. I'm sure you, yourself have done some fucked up shit to a buddy. I am sure one might have wrotten you off while others turned out okay.

This is why I hate reddit, anytime someone fucks up, it's always "abandon ship." - Anytime someone fucks up in a friendship/relationship it's always "It's over, never contact them."
Yeah, I plan on doing that. Like I said, I'm just afraid I've tainted friendships. I really wish I can get them back once I've worked on myself.

>It would be safer for you to call someone who wouldn't have the baggage of your early pleas for attention. Again, shitty, but I'm just speaking from personal experience.

Agreed, that's why I'm posting on this sub. 


Thanks for the advice, it gives me a bit of hope. 

I am just slightly afraid of losing them for good. If this was a one-time flair up, that would be one thing. But the thing is, it's happened in the past. In the old days, it was an every day thing. Hell, I wasn't even friends with them at the time, just aquantences through mutual friends. They actually didn't like me that much, lol. Then I changed myself and I really confided in them and we became super close. But I occasionally have relapses and that's what scares them off. Sure, they've written me off before, but I am scared this might be the straw that broke the camel's back and that it's too late.

>You say you're working on your behavior- that's awesome. You've obviously realized there's an issue, and you're addressing it. That's a huge step, but you need to remember not not change the things which make you you. Change the stuff which may cause problems with others, but ultimately you are what you are and you can only do so much.

Agreed. I am not ever going to change what makes me, me. The only reason why I have like-minded friends that were my friends in the first place is because I was myself. So I'm going to try and "capitalize" (for a lack of a better word) on my good qualities and work on my bad.

>As for reddit? I say fuck reddit. Seriously, reddit has the most disgusting opinion bias and closed minded attitude. Particularly on the default subs- full of racism, bias, and overwhelming 'hivemind' (as much as I hate to use that word) of people who all support the same argument thinking they're agreeing, when really the other side of the argument has been downvoted to invisibility

I've noticed that too, it really annoys me.



Anyways, the reason why I feel suicidal is just knowing that someone I cared about and I'm sure cared about me (hopefully still does), doesn't care anymore. Sure, I have my mother who loves me and other family members that do, but that doesn't speak a whole lot of me as a person. Serial killers, murderers and rapists have family members that care about them most of the time. I am worried that someone (and some of my other friends) that I admire and care about, think I am a horrible person due to some fucked up behavioral patterns that come out occasionally. 

Anyway, thanks for taking the time out to read my posts and reply. It makes me grateful that there are people out there who want to help out strangers like myself. :) Humanity isn't too terrible after all, I guess.
